dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The cluster contains 17 annual renewals, all from DLR-104 and DLR-219, posted in one 21:00 batch | recharges.csv | High"
"Annual rows matched the dealer import log exactly, including row counts and dollar amounts | recharges.csv and dealer_import_log.csv | High"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "It represents genuine annual-plan renewals uploaded together as a month-end batch by West dealers DLR-104 and DLR-219."
"The only concern is that a report based on posting date may show a misleading spike."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "The revenue-recognition basis is not established by these files."
"The contract allowing monthly batch submission is also asserted in the email and has not been independently verified."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Recompute the trend report using effective_event_date instead of posted_at, or clearly label month-end batch postings."
"Confirm the revenue-recognition rule with Revenue Assurance and verify the West-dealer mapping before making any external statement."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Do not reverse or hold the postings because the transactions are unique, genuine, and reconciled."
"A pipeline defect is rejected because all 41 import files were reconciled, accepted rows matched received rows, and the reconciliation difference was zero."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The 31-May cluster does not indicate duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, or a pipeline defect" is somewhat too definitive because unique IDs, pricing, and reconciliation do not by themselves rule out unauthorized, invalid, or deliberately misclassified renewals.

"It represents genuine annual-plan renewals" overstates what the cited file checks establish; they support uniqueness, pricing consistency, and reconciliation, but not full contractual validity or authorization.

"Therefore, no material escalation is required" is reasonable for operational posting handling, but should remain conditional on confirming the revenue-recognition basis and dealer authorization/contract terms.
The evidence table cites files at a broad level but does not provide row identifiers, query logic, or the effective-date distribution needed for fully reproducible verification.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst appropriately considered duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, and a pipeline defect, and identified the important alternative that posting-time batching distorts trend analytics. The main alternative not fully ruled out is that the rows are unique and technically reconciled but unauthorized, invalid, or otherwise misclassified renewals; the email and pricing consistency are corroboration rather than proof of that issue being absent.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a reproducible cohort-level reconciliation showing the 17 annual rows, their unique source_event_ids, effective_event_date versus posted_at distribution, and zero cash/entitlement difference, while explicitly making the no-escalation decision conditional on confirmation of authorization and revenue-recognition rules.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Observed facts: South cases fell from 157 in May to 104 in June, while control regions stayed broadly flat."
"The containment dashboard excludes pre-auth sessions, making NOVA containment appear as 64.8% instead of 56.1% using all sessions."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Inference: fewer CareDesk cases mainly means fewer contacts reached the case-creation stage."
"Causal claim: the data supports that authentication defects and reporting rules contributed to the decline, but it does not prove that every missing case represents an unresolved complaint."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "The hypothesis that all the improvement is fake is also rejected. NOVA introduced genuine self-service for simple balance and pack-information requests."
"However, the exact customer-level effect remains unknown: sessions are not the same as people, and some callers may have succeeded after retrying."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Pause national expansion and keep the South pilot under controlled observation."
"Recalculate containment using all sessions, publish pre-authentication failures alongside CareDesk cases, and track repeat contacts and unresolved subscribers."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Do not reverse the pilot or declare it a failure."
"What customer-level metric will be used to decide whether national expansion is safe, including repeat contacts, unresolved issues, and all-contact resolution?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Some improvement is genuine because balance_check and pack_info self-service stages are new under NOVA." The existence of new stages demonstrates changed capability, but does not by itself establish successful resolution or improved customer experience.

"The evidence indicates a mixed outcome" is reasonable as a working interpretation, but the submission does not provide direct linked journey outcomes proving the size of either successful deflection or unresolved friction.

"Authentication failures tripled" is a shorthand for the change from 7.9% to 24.0%; the submission should clarify that these are rates and distinguish failure counts from pre-authentication session endings.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest benign alternative: some of the decline may reflect genuine self-service success rather than only measurement failure, and a company-wide seasonal explanation is less likely because control regions were stable. It also preserved the possibility that callers succeeded after retrying. It did not explicitly propose sampled call listening, which would help distinguish failed authentication, abandonment, and non-complaint IVR use.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Build a linked, customer-level journey outcome analysis for IVR attempts—authentication result, case creation, retries, other-channel contacts, resolution, and repeat contact—and validate ambiguous abandonment cases with sampled call listening before making any national expansion decision.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv`, the four rows, `inverter_id`, `timestamp_local`, `impact_mw`, `cleared`, `duration_min`, and `severity`.
It explicitly separates “Fact,” “Inference,” and “Unknown,” which distinguishes observations from conclusions.

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: It cross-checks event count, inverter IDs, impact, cleared status, duration, and severity rather than relying on event names alone.
It tests the plausible alternative that the export is incomplete or filtered and recommends checking export coverage.

The reasoning that an active failure would require non-zero impact, uncleared status, critical severity, recurrence, or long duration is somewhat too categorical; those indicators would strengthen the hypothesis but are not necessary conditions for a failure.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission labels the event-level conclusion “High confidence” but the fleet-coverage conclusion “Medium confidence.”
It explicitly states that the four rows cannot establish that all inverters are safe and identifies export completeness as the key unknown.
It proposes the smallest decision-changing check: confirm whether the export is complete and unfiltered for the intended fleet and period.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation not to escalate is tied to zero MW impact, cleared status, short durations, low severities, and lack of recurrence within the extract.
The proposed follow-up—confirming completeness and requesting the full export only if necessary—is proportionate and operationally useful.
It avoids inventing a plant problem from a short communications warning.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion that the supplied records do not show an active or recurring equipment problem is consistent with four cleared, zero-impact events lasting 1–7 minutes.
The conclusion is appropriately limited by the statement that export completeness is unknown.
The submission correctly says that names such as `COMM_LINK_WARN`, `FAN_SPEED_HIGH`, and `DC_INPUT_CHECK` alone do not establish failure, intent, or commercial loss.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “No recurrence” is supported only within the four supplied records; it cannot establish absence of recurrence outside the extract.

The statement that an active inverter failure would require at least one non-zero impact, uncleared status, critical/error severity, recurrence, or long duration is overstated. A real but transient or unmeasured failure could have none of those fields.
“If it is complete, no more analysis is needed” is slightly broader than the evidence supports; it is defensible for escalation triage, but not as a general statement that the fleet is safe.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The events could be transient communications or telemetry-quality warnings, or isolated short-lived inverter conditions that cleared before producing measurable MW impact. This alternative does not currently justify escalation, but it would merit a low-priority quality check if the export is complete or if similar events recur.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the scope explicit in the rejection: say the records do not justify escalation or support an active recurring problem in the supplied extract, rather than implying that failure is ruled out, and identify export completeness as the sole next check.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Recomputing the headline figures from dispatch_blocks.csv gives Rs 662,444 on 28 May and Rs 453,086 on 29 May" is tied to daily penalty totals and the impact note.
The 17.5% estimate is explicitly tied to 29-May base_schedule_mw, submitted schedule, actual generation, and penalty fields.
The submission cross-references dispatch_blocks.csv, DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf, and the impact note rather than relying on the headline alone.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It distinguishes the different-day comparison from the same-day base-versus-submitted comparison: "The stronger same-day comparison uses the 29-May base_schedule_mw as the no-pilot baseline while holding actual generation fixed."
It checks banded penalties and STOW concentration, firmware differences, schedule-change timing, and net commercial value.
It rejects the fabricated-number hypothesis by reproducing the totals while rejecting the stronger causal interpretation of 31.6%.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "The defensible surviving claim is a 17.5% within-day reduction on one pilot day, not a general 31.6% effect" is appropriately scoped.
It explicitly identifies unresolved issues: generalization, whether revision preceded actual generation, and net commercial value.
It labels the same-day result an "estimated 17.5% effect" rather than treating the baseline as definitive causal proof.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to continue only as a limited evaluation and not expand follows from the one-day evidence and causal uncertainty.
The proposed next test repeats the same-day calculation across pre-defined high-wind stow days, controls firmware, and measures both penalty and net commercial value.
It preserves operationally relevant constraints by requiring evidence of ex-ante scheduling and positive net value before expansion.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion directly notices that 31.6% compares 28 May with 29 May and retains the smaller same-day benefit rather than dismissing the pilot entirely.
"Report the 17.5% within-day result, not the 31.6% cross-day figure" matches the strongest supported interpretation of the supplied evidence.
The submission does not claim that the pilot caused a general reduction or that lower DSM penalty proves better commercial performance.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Calling base_schedule_mw a "no-pilot baseline" or "same-day counterfactual" is reasonable for the requested analysis but remains an assumption: the submission itself does not establish that this schedule was generated independently of pilot information or that it would have been submitted absent the pilot.

The phrase "same-day counterfactual shows an estimated 17.5% reduction" could still be read too causally; the comparison holds actual generation fixed but does not by itself establish ex-ante comparability or eliminate schedule-selection effects.

The statement that 28 May was the "highest-penalty conventional day" is reported as sourced, but the underlying file rows are not reproduced in the submission, so the evaluator cannot independently verify the calculation from the text alone.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 17.5% difference may reflect a useful ex-post schedule-reconstruction or mechanical penalty effect without being a fully identified causal pilot effect. The base schedule could differ from the submitted schedule for reasons related to forecasts, operational decisions, or pilot targeting; repeated pre-specified same-day comparisons with ex-ante timestamps are needed to separate those explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Establish the timing and provenance of base_schedule_mw and submitted_schedule_mw for each revised block, then repeat the fixed-actual-generation comparison over multiple pre-specified high-wind events with firmware held constant and net energy value included.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The declaration records tariff code `90211000` for P1001" with the specific location "`declaration.pdf`; goods/classification field for packet CH-2025-000522".
"`90211000` is the approved Swiss code for P1001" with the specific source "`country_tariff_matrix.xlsx`; **Swiss Matrix**, P1001 row, Approved CN8 and effective-date columns".
"The packet has a separate quantity/value inconsistency" with references to "`commercial_invoice.pdf`; Qty 10" and "`air_waybill.pdf`; 4 pieces".

The submission identifies precise files, rows, fields and dates, but generally reports source contents rather than quoting the underlying documents or fully distinguishing a commercial matrix from an official customs ruling.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "The hypothesis that the declaration contains a likely tariff-code error is rejected" because "The declared `90211000` matches the current Swiss authority exactly".
"The hypothesis that `90211090` is the universally correct code is also rejected" by testing jurisdiction and effective date.
"The hypothesis that the packet is completely clean is not established" because the submission separately examines invoice, line-value and AWB discrepancies.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The decision is appropriately limited: "Do not escalate CH-2025-000522 as a likely declaration error" rather than declaring the entire packet compliant.
The submission explicitly identifies uncertainty and requests "the official Swiss customs classification or ruling applicable to the exact product and entry date, 2025-11-04".

It appropriately states that "The packet is completely clean is not established," but the phrase "matches the current Swiss authority exactly" is stronger than the cited matrix evidence unless that matrix is itself authoritative.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains the mechanism as "comparing codes from different jurisdictional systems" and distinguishes Swiss code `90211000` from a "Helios commercial/EU CN8 reference".
It traces data lineage by stating that `90211090` is the "Helios commercial commodity code, not customs-ruling status" and cites the product master Read Me.

It also incorporates temporal behavior: "The EU code itself changed from `90211010` to `90211090` on 2025-07-01," though it gives limited detail about the operational process that generated the flag or the incentives behind the mismatch.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The recommended disposition is proportionate: "Do not escalate ... as a likely declaration error" while preserving review of the separate discrepancy.
The submission proposes reversible verification: "If it confirms `90211000`, the code-mismatch issue can be closed ... If it specifies another Swiss code, reopen the classification review."

It requests a "corrected invoice or written supplier/broker reconciliation" and requires reconciliation of "actual shipped quantity, unit value, line value, and why the AWB shows 4 pieces while the invoice shows quantity 10."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The declaration uses Swiss code `90211000`, which matches the current Swiss tariff matrix for P1001" is well tied to the cited matrix, but calling it the "approved Swiss code" and saying it "matches the current Swiss authority exactly" may overstate what a tariff matrix proves unless the file is an official authoritative source.

"The flagged `90211090` is a Helios commercial/EU CN8 reference, not a Swiss customs ruling" is plausible and specifically sourced to the product master and Read Me, but the submission does not independently establish that no separate Swiss ruling exists.
Calling the invoice/AWB discrepancy a "valuation/quantity issue" is somewhat broad; the cited evidence establishes an inconsistency requiring reconciliation, not yet an actual valuation violation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss matrix may be a reference or internal operational table rather than binding customs authority, so `90211000` could still be incorrect for the exact product or entry date. In addition, the invoice quantity/value and AWB quantity mismatch could indicate a broader shipment or declaration problem even if the tariff-code comparison is benign.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quote or attach the decisive Swiss Matrix row and its authority/status metadata, then explicitly reconcile whether it is binding official guidance or an internal reference before asserting that `90211000` matches Swiss authority exactly.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Preference is claimed for P1006, but supplier support is not linked" is tied to "declaration.pdf — preference field; review_note.txt — supplier support not linked in ClearView."
"SUP-02/P1006 has Irish origin, but its declaration expired before entry" is tied to "supplier_origin_register.csv — SUP-02/P1006 row: valid_to = 2025-07-31; entry date = 2025-09-18."
The submission identifies limitations by stating that "the supplier register may be incomplete and a valid document may exist outside the register."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission explicitly rejects the hypothesis that "ERP shows US origin, so the preference claim is definitely false" because "ERP was not designed to prove preferential origin."
It also rejects route-based reasoning: "The route to Ireland proves Irish origin" is rejected because "the air waybill shows only the logistics route."
The reasoning distinguishes absence of support from falsity: "The claim is not proven false because the supplier register may be incomplete and a valid document may exist outside the register."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The conclusion is appropriately qualified: "The preferential-origin claim ... is not supported by the available evidence" rather than declaring it false.
The submission assigns "High" confidence to directly documented facts and "Medium" confidence to the inference that the claim is unsupported but "not conclusively false."
It identifies precise missing evidence, including "A current supplier declaration or valid origin proof for P1006 covering the 2025-09-18 entry" and "The preference agreement or rule being used."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains a system limitation: "ERP origin is US but does not prove preferential origin" because "Helios was never designed to prove preference."
It identifies data-lineage and workflow limitations: "supplier support is not linked in ClearView" and "register is not always updated."
It recognizes that supplier identity and transaction scope matter by requesting "The actual sourcing supplier for this shipment" and evidence that "covers the 2025-09-18 entry."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The proposed interim control is proportionate and reversible: "hold the preference claim and treat the line as non-preferential/MFN for now."

The submission requests corroborating evidence before final disposition: "Request the current supplier declaration, the applicable preference rule and confirmation that the document covers the 2025-09-18 entry."

It provides conditional resolution paths: "If valid origin proof is produced and matches the applicable rule, accept the preference claim. If no valid proof is produced, withdraw or correct the preference indicator."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The tariff code is not the issue" is too categorical: showing that 90211090 appears in the EU tariff matrix does not establish that tariff classification, the applicable preference agreement, or the origin rule is irrelevant.
"The issue is duty-neutral" relies on the declared 0.0% duty and does not fully address possible compliance, reporting, audit, or future-duty consequences if the preference status is corrected.

"Treat the line as non-preferential/MFN for now" is a reasonable conservative control, but the MFN characterization is not established until the applicable tariff treatment and preference agreement are confirmed.

The statement that "the only Irish-origin declaration found" is carefully limited by the register caveat, but it should expressly distinguish the register search result from a complete supplier-document search.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A valid, current supplier declaration or other legally sufficient origin proof may exist outside ClearView or the supplier register, possibly from the actual shipment supplier rather than SUP-02. The expired SUP-02 record therefore shows that one located document cannot cover the entry, but does not establish that the preference claim is invalid or fraudulent. Conversely, Irish manufacturing or an Ireland route alone would still not establish preferential origin.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Tie the proposed treatment to the specific preference agreement and origin criterion, then verify the actual shipment supplier and search the authoritative procurement/category records for transaction-specific proof before characterizing the line as MFN or requiring correction.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "185 of 262 release timestamps, or 70.6%, are exactly 02:10:00, matching the QCore daily snapshot time."
"Receipt-to-release is 45.5 hours mean, while the SOP evidence-available-to-release measure is 26.9 hours mean and 21.3 hours median."
"The arithmetic is clean; the main problem is timestamp meaning and freshness."

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "This suggests that many timestamps record the snapshot boundary rather than the actual release time."
"If the live times vary during the day while the extract shows 02:10:00 for all of them, the extract contains a snapshot-time artifact."
"A fresher, aligned extract or event-level QCore log [is needed] to remove the LabTrack 48-hour lag and QCore daily-snapshot lag."

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "This suggests"
"COA MISSING and INDEX_PENDING may be caused by CertVault index lag"
"A live CertVault check [is needed] before treating it as a control failure."

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do not publish the QC cycle-time KPI from this extract yet."
"The one-and-a-half-day claim is not a reliable KPI."
"The agreed metric definition: evidence-available-to-disposition, included dispositions, and exclusion of open complex exceptions."

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "The data is broken and should be discarded. Rejected because the arithmetic is clean."
"The KPI represents the current queue. Rejected because all 42 latest HOLD batches have null release timestamps."
"COA MISSING proves certificates were absent when batches were released. Rejected because CertVault is a nightly index."

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "The single decisive next check is to select 5–10 rows ... and compare those timestamps with the actual disposition times in live QCore."
"A fresher, aligned extract or event-level QCore log"
"The agreed metric definition"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The submission treats `lab_complete_ts` as the SOP's evidence-available timestamp without demonstrating that lab completion is equivalent to all required evidence being available.

"Many timestamps record the snapshot boundary" is a well-supported hypothesis but is not established until live QCore or event-log comparison confirms whether 02:10 is an interface commit, scheduled release, or extraction default.

The 5.5-hour median and 22-of-23 target result are calculated after removing suspected artifacts and excluding exceptions; they should not be presented as an operational KPI until the timestamp semantics and inclusion rules are validated.

Calling the live-QCore sample the "single decisive next check" under-prioritizes the event/decision timestamp definition and the need to confirm whether the QCore and LabTrack extracts represent a coherent snapshot.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10:00 concentration may reflect a legitimate scheduled or batch release process rather than a pure snapshot artifact, while the extract's apparent delay may also be amplified by the non-coherent LabTrack and QCore refresh times. In that case, the data may still measure an interface-release process, but not the intended decision-to-release cycle.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly map the SOP's "required evidence available" event to a source field or event-log timestamp, then obtain a small, time-aligned sample containing evidence-available, disposition-decision, and QCore interface-commit times. This would distinguish workflow delay from interface/extract timing before any filtered KPI is published.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "There are 24 open requests worth $166,495.60... the buckets are 8 actionable, 12 needs check, and 4 not transferable"; source fields are specified as `part_requests.csv`, `spare_parts.csv`, and `part_restrictions.csv`.
"HA-0022 has on-hand quantity 3 but `available_qty_global = −1`; ME-0006 has on-hand quantity 1 but availability −1" with the specific fields and `maintenance_email.txt` identified.
"The global stock view is dated 2026-06-26 and refreshed monthly..." citing `source_freshness.csv`.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The semantic-search pilot is useful for discovering candidates, but it is not a transfer approver."
"A matching description or part family proves interchangeability." Rejected using blank manufacturer numbers, revision mismatch, and site-specific restrictions.
"`available_qty_global = −1` means the stock is unavailable." Rejected by contrasting on-hand quantities with the email warning about lagging global availability.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "8 of 24... are actionable now, 12... need a specific check, and 4... are not transferable."
"live reservation status is unclear" and "medium for present-day stock" are claim-specific uncertainty statements.
"Because the global stock snapshot is stale, even the 8 actionable matches should be confirmed..."

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "I would not cancel all 24 external purchase requests based only on search hits."
"I would proceed with the 8 clean transfers, investigate the 12 conditional cases, and keep buying the 4 servo drives."
"The firm opportunity is approximately $20.5k, not the apparent $166.5k."

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission explicitly rejects five alternatives, including "The search found a match, so it should be transferred," "The search creates $166.5k of confirmed savings," and "`available_qty_global = −1` means the stock is unavailable."
"A live reservation review could change the servo-drive decision only if the safety-critical reservation has genuinely been released; otherwise the four external buys should continue."

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Confirming the manufacturer part numbers for the 11 blank requests"
"Checking live local stock and reservation records for HA-0022 and ME-0006"
"Engineering confirmation that VLV-3722 revision A and revision B are interchangeable"
"Receiving-site qualification approval" and a "live reservation review" are targeted evidence requests tied to specific decision changes.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Calling the 8 matches "actionable now" is somewhat overstated because the submission also acknowledges that the global stock snapshot is about four weeks old and that live reservation status is unresolved for some inventory; they are better described as policy-qualified candidates pending live confirmation.

"The firm opportunity is approximately $20.5k" is directionally well supported as a currently qualified candidate value, but it is not fully firm until the stale inventory and reservation data are refreshed.

The statement that all 11 blank-part-number requests could move toward actionability after identity confirmation does not establish that quantity, revision, qualification, and reservation gates will also pass.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 8 clean matches represent a well-screened candidate opportunity rather than guaranteed current transfers. The stale MaintStar snapshot and possible local reservations could reduce even the $20.5k opportunity, while resolving blank identities, revision equivalence, or site qualification could expand the opportunity beyond the currently actionable bucket.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Refresh live inventory, reservation, and qualification data for the eight proposed transfers before authorizing them, explicitly converting the current 8/12/4 classification from a stale-snapshot assessment into a verified operational decision.
